newsitem.title: PERU: Peru September inflation falls to 0.32 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru September inflation falls to 0.32 percent.

text.p: Consumer prices rose 0.32 percent in September, compared with a 0.4 percent rise in the same month last year and a 0.92 percent rised in August, the government said on Tuesday.
Accumulated inflation in the first nine months of was 9.19 percent, up from 7.8 percent in the same period last year, according to the National Institute of Information and Statistics (INEI).
Peruvian inflation fell to 10.2 percent in 1995 from 15.4 percent in 1994. The 1995 figure was the lowest in 23 years.

Although the government originally hoped for single-digit inflation in 1996 and agreed with the International Monetary Fund on a target of 9.5-11.5 percent, President Alberto Fujimori's latest estimate is 12 percent.
The government estimates accumulated inflation will be nine percent in 1997 and will drop to "the level of industrialized countries" by the year 2000.
